subject: environmental-science
title: The Carbon Cycle Re-balanced
welcome_lead: Atmosphere, oceans and biosphere — track the world's largest carbon ledger.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on the global carbon cycle and reservoirs.
final_note: Reservoirs are vast, fluxes are tiny — but tiny fluxes accumulated for centuries change the climate.

walkthroughs.body_html: Oceans dwarf atmospheric and terrestrial pools. Yet small annual transfers between them dominate climate change.
Global GPP ~120 Gt C yr⁻¹ is balanced by respiration. Fossil fuel combustion adds ~10 Gt C yr⁻¹ — a small but cumulative perturbation.
Cold polar water dissolves more CO₂ (solubility pump). Sinking organic detritus exports C to depth (biological pump).

mcqs.q: Which reservoir contains the most carbon globally?
options: Oceans (~38 000 Gt C)
Atmosphere (~870 Gt C)
Soils (~1500 Gt C)
Vegetation (~500 Gt C)

mcqs.q: Average atmospheric CO₂ residence time is approximately:
options: 5 years
100 years
1 year
1000 years

mcqs.q: What process moves carbon from the atmosphere into plants?
options: Photosynthesis.
Because plants only use carbon.
Respiration.
Decomposition.

mcqs.q: Why is burning fossil fuels considered to disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: Decomposition.
It creates new carbon that did not exist before.
It removes carbon permanently.
It releases carbon stored for millions of years much faster than the cycle can absorb.

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: Decomposition.
Because plants only use carbon.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.
N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.
